name: IA-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
McGowan's large fundraising and outside-spending edge over Dawson
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: This is an open seat in a district that leans Republican by about fifteen points, and no polling or expert ratings exist to move the picture. Chris McGowan has far outraised David Dawson and drawn outside support, while markets price a Republican win at roughly 94%, so the forecast sits a few points beyond the district's baseline lean.
model.watch: A competitive or fractured Republican primary, or a late Democratic fundraising surge, could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Iowa's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, and Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor leaves it open without an incumbent on the ballot. Republican Chris McGowan enters the general election with a clear financial advantage, having raised roughly five times as much as Democrat David Dawson and benefited from outside spending, while Dawson has limited cash on hand and no outside support on record.

With no public polling and no expert ratings of the race, the outlook rests on the district's strong partisan lean and the candidates' resources. Markets price a Republican win at about 94%. The seat remains very likely to stay in Republican hands, though an open seat carries somewhat more uncertainty than a race with an incumbent defending it.
